newsitem.title: USA: Natural gas futures seen moving moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: Natural gas futures seen moving moderately lower.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open relatively steady but trend moderately lower through the day with little heating demand and recent significant storage injections, industry sources said.

Traders said October futures were expected to open slightly above Thursday's close of $2.137 per million British thermal units with over-the-counter discussion pegged in the $2.13-2.16 range, the brokers and marketers said.
Although the opening call was for slightly higher, traders were bearish overall.
In ACCESS futures, November traded up 1.3 cents at $2.15, with bids standing at $2.146 and offers at $2.154 per mmBtu.
A moderate downturn Friday was expected to continue into next week, the sources said.
"The longer term forecast (for gas) would be down, there is less and less chance of hurricane danger as we get closer to winter," one sources said.
Technically, traders pegged November support in the $2.00 area, with resistance at Thursday's high of $2.18 and then at the recent high of $2.305.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
